name: AI-assisted SDLC

card.question: Can we trust what the agent built?
card.title: AI-assisted SDLC: engineering with agents
card.description: What it takes to delegate software work to AI agents and still know it works: specifications, harnesses, deterministic checks and human approval. Start with Part 1.

excerpts.1: “Build a booking API” is a wish. Twenty years from ARM assembly to AI agents, and the one question that has not changed: how do we know it works?
excerpts.2: A prompt describes what to build. A specification also says what must never happen. Turning “Build a booking API” into four testable invariants, and why the second question mattered most.
excerpts.3: The same model behaves very differently depending on what surrounds it. Context, tools, feedback and recovery: what a harness has to do, and why every part of it encodes a doubt about the model.
excerpts.4: A rule in a prompt is a request. A rule in the system is a control. What an agent may read, change and execute, and what stops it when it tries anyway.
excerpts.5: The AI reviewer scored the code 9/10. The test proved it double-booked a room ten times. Both were honest. Where model judgement helps, and why a deterministic check must win.
excerpts.6: A person clicking “Approve” on fifty green pull requests is a ritual, not a control. Which changes need a person, and what that person needs to see.
excerpts.7: Specifications, a harness, enforced permissions, deterministic checks and a human gate, brought together into one delivery flow that produces code and the evidence that it is safe to ship.
